why: A printing helper of Java that purity's list does not know: it lays a map literal out as Map.of(k, v, ...) up to the ten pairs Map.of takes and as Map.ofEntries(Map.entry(k, v), ...) past them (ts/src/helpers/opExample.ts javaMap). It reads no model and decides nothing shown; the old java components used the same helper (through javaMapOf).

Not in JAVA_CORE: JAVA_CORE is the constant 'core' (utility_java.ts, the subpackage Main_java's Folder writes). purity's fnBody looks for the first '{' after a const that is not an arrow function, so it reads the body of mavenGroupId, the next function in the file, as JAVA_CORE's. The line is mavenGroupId's own (the Maven group id, which the hook does not use).

Not in JAVA_ENTITY: JAVA_ENTITY is the constant 'entity' (utility_java.ts, the subpackage EntityBase_java's and Entity_java's Folder writes, which the hook gives as names.entity at v3.4). As for JAVA_CORE above, purity's fnBody reads the body of mavenGroupId, the next function in the file, as the constant's; the line is mavenGroupId's own, which the hook does not use.

The hook neither imports nor calls mavenGroupId: purity reached it through the misread body of the constant JAVA_CORE (see the entry above). It is Package_java's Maven group id (com.<org>), which no page prints.

The java generator's own rule for a Map.of argument (ts/src/helpers/opExample.ts javaMapItems: a member whose type is NULL is left out, because Map.of throws NullPointerException on a null value). ReadmeEntity_java, ReadmeHowto_java, ReadmeTopTest_java and utility_java's javaListMatch call it, and so did the three old components. The provider passes it the literal type of each entry the statement already holds; it reads no model and adds nothing to what is shown: get() on the map reads the left-out member as null.

check: import from outside the printing helpers
why: The java generator's one table of example literals (utility_java.ts javaLit), which ReadmeEntity_java, ReadmeHowto_java and ReadmeTopTest_java also call. ts/test/generate.test.ts ('java and scala write example literals from one table each') fails while any other java file holds such a table, and the provider's own copy had lost the rule that keeps a null-only member out of Map.of. javaLit takes the canonical type key and the placeholder the statement already holds; it reads no model.
